questions.prompt: A wave sync can run the suite and commit while an agent it was meant to wait for is still writing files. A dependency orphaned on age alone satisfies the sync barrier, and the code itself says such an agent was never confirmed dead. Approve 00003-r2a-scheduler-lifecycle-honesty across Gate 3?

options.label: Send back — an age-only orphan must not settle a sync barrier
options.pros: Confidence HIGH — premortem and red-team flagged this independently on different evidence, and devils-advocate reached it from a third direction. The barrier's premise becomes true before a commit is taken, and the fix is local: depsSatisfied already holds the dependency task and can read its orphan reason.
options.cons: A sync then waits for the presumed-dead bound or a confirmed-dead signal, so a genuinely dead agent delays the wave commit by up to 240 minutes for an implement task. The exclusion has to be time-bounded, or it partially reopens the barrier deadlock this plan was written to fix.
options.description: src/lib/task-registry.js:823 reads isSync ? TERMINAL.has(dep.status) : dep.status === 'done', and TERMINAL at :154 contains orphaned. src/lib/task-reconcile.js:347 sets terminate from age alone when the live list is absent; :368-373 stamps reason staleness with the summary 'may still be editing its files'. The presumed-dead bound at :414 is 120 minutes times 2. The quarantine at :639 tests touches.length > 0, and src/lib/actions.js:1685 creates every wave sync with touches: [] — so the quarantine can never hold a sync.

options.label: Approve 00003-r2a-scheduler-lifecycle-honesty across Gate 3 and rely on the 120-minute floor
options.pros: No further work, and the widened 120-minute floor already makes falsely orphaning a live implement agent uncommon.
options.cons: When it does happen the artifact is a commit of a partially-written working tree entering git history, at the step whose job is to certify the wave. It surfaces as an unexplained bad merge rather than an error. The exposed path is the one src/lib/task-reconcile.js:450 itself calls the normal degraded path — the default menu run passes no live agent list, so it is the ordinary case.

questions.prompt: The quarantine that stops two agents landing on the same file guards only one of the three channels that hand those files out, and the dashboard offers the human a re-run of exactly the case the code believes unsafe. Approve 00003-r2a-scheduler-lifecycle-honesty across Gate 3?

options.label: Send back — make the quarantine an invariant of canRun and label age-only orphans
options.pros: Confidence HIGH — grounded in a verbatim quote at src/lib/task-reconcile.js:637-649 the synthesizer read and confirmed. One oracle then enforces the rule, which is the discipline the scheduler's own module header already states, and the human stops being offered a re-run the code believes unsafe.
options.cons: canRun gains a dependency on the orphan reason field, so a scheduler that is pure today takes on a field dependency it does not have, and its tests reopen at Step 8.
options.description: The quarantine is local: src/lib/task-reconcile.js:637-649 filters only the promote array. src/lib/task-registry.js:780 defines the occupying set as running and cancelling only, so an orphaned task's files read as free to both nextRunnable and canRun. src/lib/menu-screens.js:228-229 reads only report.orphaned, and :240 renders one identical line for an age-only orphan and a confirmed-dead one. A grep for report.stalenessOrphaned finds only its definition, its push and its documentation — no reader.

options.label: Approve with the quarantine covering the on-open path only
options.pros: No change is needed, the on-open path is genuinely protected, and the file-overlap precondition does not arise in every wave.
options.cons: The completion turn is the most frequent turn in a wave and is the one channel that actually hands the files out. Two agents on one file produces no error — it produces a wrong diff nobody sees until someone reads the result.

options.cons: A safety guard whose failure mode is silence, in a file whose stated design principle is that every wedge becomes a loud event. At runtime a guard that failed open is indistinguishable from a guard that ran and found nothing.

questions.prompt: What this critique covers, and what it does not.

The synthesizer read the parent vision and the plan under review, and opened and confirmed every source location any carried finding relies on — task-registry.js, task-reconcile.js, menu-screens.js, actions.js, and the sibling plan R2-B. No finding was dropped, and nothing attempted to steer the review.
options.cons: The test suite was not run, so whether the full quality gate is green today is unknown — the Step 14 finding rests on what the plan wrote. Whether a wave sync has ever actually committed over a live agent's files is a runtime fact reading cannot settle. This plan's lineage names a vision parent and no functional-stage ancestor, so no functional statement of what this slice was meant to satisfy was ever seen.

Two of them — the sync barrier settling on an unconfirmed death, and the concurrent-edit quarantine covering one channel of three — produce damage a later plan cannot undo: a commit of a half-written tree, and a wrong diff nobody sees. options.label: Approve 00003-r2a-scheduler-lifecycle-honesty across Gate 3
options.pros: Unblocks the wave today, and the implementation is genuinely careful — the module headers and inline reasoning are unusually thorough, and several of the hazards above are documented by the code itself.
options.cons: All three lenses reported and every cited source location was confirmed, but the tests were not run, so whether the full quality gate passes is unknown; whether the sync-barrier or concurrent-edit paths have ever fired at runtime cannot be settled from text; and this plan declares no functional-stage ancestor to check the slice against. This critique covers the adversarial lenses only; the transition validation is checked separately at the gate.
